Zarasai New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Utenos apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Zarasai was the birthplace of the painter Yehuda Pen (1854), who later established an art school in Vitebsk that became the first artistic home for many notable artists, including Marc Chagall. Unlike most other Litvak cemeteries documented in this collection, this cemetery was never closed during the Soviet era — it has remained active and well-maintained by the town continuously since opening in the early 1930s, with its latest grave dating to 1986. Unusually for a Lithuanian Jewish cemetery, some of its tombstones are decorated with photographs of the deceased, a style more typical of later Soviet-era memorials than prewar Jewish tradition.
